One of my friend’s grandfathers was diagnosed with cancer and we were referred to Dr. Rakesh Neve at Lifepoint Hospital. After looking at the reports, he confidently told us not to worry and said, “He will go home walking the same way he came, without a scratch.” Based on those assurances, we agreed to proceed with surgery.

After surgery, we were told everything had gone well and that he would be discharged in a few days. A few days turned into 28 days. Every time we asked why he was still admitted, we were given vague explanations—more observation, physiotherapy, additional tests, scans, IV medications, and other procedures. Throughout this period, nobody clearly communicated what was actually happening.

The most disturbing part was the complete lack of transparency. We repeatedly asked for the medical file because we wanted a second opinion, but were continuously denied. We were even told we could not take photographs of the records. Only after significant pressure was applied were we finally given access.

We then met CEO Anjali Pradhan, who questioned why we had escalated the matter instead of approaching management directly. She promised a meeting later that day with Dr. Rakesh Neve and ICU doctor Pawan Chaudhary. However, when we returned, both Ms. Pradhan and Dr. Chaudhary left the hospital without meeting us. It genuinely appeared as though they were avoiding difficult questions.

When we finally met Dr. Neve and asked what had gone wrong, his response was shocking: “I don’t have answers to this. I don’t know what to say.” This was the same doctor who had earlier assured us there was nothing to worry about.

On the 28th day, we were told the patient could be discharged, but only after clearing all pending bills. We paid immediately. While leaving the hospital, he suddenly developed a high fever and severe shivering. He was re-admitted, moved to the ICU, put on a ventilator the next day, and passed away the following day.

We understand that not every patient can be saved. Cancer is a serious disease and complications can happen. What is unacceptable is the lack of honesty, communication, empathy, and transparency shown throughout the entire process.

To make matters worse, we were initially told the total expense would be around ₹4.5 lakh. The final bill exceeded ₹8.5 lakh. After everything that happened, the hospital offered a discount of only ₹30,000.

The names I will never forget are Dr. Rakesh Neve, Anjali Pradhan, and Dr. Pawan Chaudhary. What hurt us most was not the outcome itself, but the way the family was treated—kept in the dark, denied information, and left without answers when we needed them the most.

I would strongly advise anyone considering Lifepoint Hospital to ask questions, demand transparency, and think very carefully before placing the life of a loved one in their hands.

I had an excellent experience with La Densitae Clinic from the beginning of my hair restoration journey until the final results.

I underwent a hair transplant a few months ago, and the entire process was smooth, professional, and well managed. The doctors patiently explained the procedure, answered all my questions, and made me feel comfortable throughout. The post-procedure follow-ups and guidance were equally impressive.

Recently, I also got Scalp Micropigmentation (SMP) done at the clinic, and it was the perfect finishing touch. The SMP blended naturally with my transplanted hair, giving my hairline a fuller, denser, and more natural appearance. The attention to detail and precision of the team was outstanding.
